:::{#thm-precision-zero-cind}
#### A zero off-diagonal element of the precision matrix means conditional independence

Let $\vX \sim \Normal_p\paren{\vecf{\mean}, \matr{\covmat}}$ with $p \ge 2$,
and let $i \ne j$.
The $(i, j)$ element of the [precision matrix](#def-precision-matrix) $\precision(\vX)$ is zero
[if and only if](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-iff) $X_i$ and $X_j$ are [conditionally independent given the continuous random vector](independence.qmd#def-cind-continuous) $\vX_{-ij}$,
that is, $\vX$ without its $i$th and $j$th elements.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-precision-matrix-inverse, the $(i, j)$ element of $\precision(\vX)$ is the [coprecision](#def-coprecision) of $X_i$ and $X_j$ given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$.
Write $v_i$ and $v_j$ for the [conditional variances](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-variance) of $X_i$ and $X_j$ given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
and $c_{ij}$ for their [conditional covariance](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cond-cov).
By @thm-mvn-conditional, given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
$\tp{(X_i, X_j)}$ has a bivariate [Gaussian distribution](#def-normal) whose [variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cov-vec-x) $\matr{S}$ [is positive definite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite),
with diagonal elements $v_i$ and $v_j$ and off-diagonal element $c_{ij}$,
and $\matr{S}$ does not depend on $\vx_{-ij}$.
A [positive definite matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite) has a positive [determinant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-determinant),
so $v_i v_j - c_{ij}^2 > 0$,
and the coprecision $-c_{ij} / (v_i v_j - c_{ij}^2)$ is zero exactly when $c_{ij} = 0$.

If $c_{ij} = 0$,
then $\matr{S}$ is diagonal,
so by @cor-mvn-uncorrelated-indpt $X_i$ and $X_j$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt) given $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
for every $\vx_{-ij}$.
That is, the [conditional density](expectation.qmd#def-cond-pdf) of $\tp{(X_i, X_j)}$ equals the conditional density of $X_i$ times the conditional density of $X_j$,
which is the factorization in the definition of [conditional independence](independence.qmd#def-cind-continuous).
Conversely, if $X_i$ and $X_j$ are [conditionally independent](independence.qmd#def-cind-continuous),
then they are independent given each $\vX_{-ij} = \vx_{-ij}$,
so by @cor-mvn-uncorrelated-indpt $c_{ij} = 0$.

:::
